added.title: Director of Engineering, Compute Cloud
added.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

As the Director of Engineering - Cloud Compute, you will play a pivotal role in building our foundational IaaS offerings and accelerate the development of our carbon-reducing, AI focused cloud platform. Leveraging your extensive experience in cloud computing, you will lead complex engineering initiatives, mentor engineers, and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable and reliable cloud compute solutions. Our customers include rapidly growing AI companies and enterprise AI teams who use our high performance GPU compute products with VPC and cluster networking technology. We’re now adding broad new compute and virtualization capabilities to meet the needs of our growing customer base.

What You'll Be Working On:

Serve as a team lead for cloud compute engineering at Crusoe Cloud, collaborating with leadership to define and implement the long-term road map and strategy for the team
Guide the engineering team through architecture decisions, design processes, design reviews, code reviews, and implementation tasks
Scale the team, including managing engineer onboarding, growing or hiring managers, and implementing team and org processes.
Stay aware of the latest trends and techniques in cloud software, incorporating these insights to maintain Crusoe’s market-leading offerings
Drive the hiring process to attract top talent, and implement strategies to retain and develop these professionals

What You'll Bring to the Team:

7+ years of engineering management experience, 10+ years of experience working in software engineering
In-depth understanding of Compute products (CPU, GPU, ASIC accelerators) and how customers consume them
Understanding of key hypervisors and virtualization technologies (eg KVM, VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V) and how they enable cloud computing.
Familiarity with AI/ML workloads and how they drive compute requirements for the cloud data center.
Proven experience in building and maintaining scalable and highly available fault-tolerant distributed systems and application architectures
Knowledge of professional software engineering practices and best practices for the full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Excellent communication and collaboration skills

Bonus Points

Proven track record of operating production infrastructure to strict SLOs and SLAs, leveraging fleet-wide observability and monitoring to drive reliability, optimization, and capacity planning
Deep expertise in Linux environments, configuration management, and modern deployment automation to ensure safe, scalable rollouts across large-scale compute fleets
Demonstrated leadership in ambiguous, fast-moving environments,bringing structure, clarity, and cross-functional alignment during periods of rapid organizational growth
Active open-source or upstream contributions to cloud infrastructure, containerization, or virtualization technologies (e.g., KVM, QEMU, containerd, Kubernetes)

General Description

JOIN OUR TEAM AS THE TRANSPORTATION ENGINEERING DIRECTOR

Pasco County is seeking a visionary, strategic, and big picture thinker to inspire and take the Pasco County Transportation Engineering Department to the next level of excellence. The people and performance focused leader must strive to get results or outcomes through the team. The Transportation Engineering Director is a highly responsible professional engineering position that leads teams of engineering, technical, field and office personnel, manages capital projects, and coordinates with various stakeholders to deliver effective and efficient transportation solutions. The department consists of approximately 75 employees and manages an annual operating budget of approximately $14 million and a five-year capital budget of approximately $547 million. This position reports directly to the Assistant County Administrator for the Public Infrastructure Branch.

Essential Job Functions

Oversees, directs, and manages the personnel of the Transportation Engineering Department. Provides employee training and counseling.
Conducts performance evaluations of employees.
Oversees the development and implementation of the department’s written standard operating procedures and administrative policies.
Participates in the development of the Five-Year Transportation Capital Improvement Plan (TCIP).
Implements and manages the TCIP.
Coordinates with external stakeholders including the Pasco County Metropolitan Planning Organization. the Florida Department of Transportation, the Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise, local municipalities, developers, consultants, community organizations and various regional and national transportation partners to support the implementation of the County’s long-range transportation plan.
Coordinates and communicates with internal teams including the County Attorney’s Office, Development Services, Pasco Utilities and Public Works for the successful delivery of TCIP projects. Manages the design and execution of transportation projects to ensure adherence to quality, budget, and timeline requirements.
Supervises project managers and is engaged in the procurement and management of professional services agreements for roadway planning and design, contract documentation and computations.
Supervises the assembly of roadway design plans, signing and pavement marking plans, signalization plans, lighting plans, scopes of work, bid packages, design exceptions and variations, and utility work schedules.
Reviews contracts with engineering consultants and construction contractors to ensure compliance with project requirements and budgets.
Reviews Engineer of Record probable cost estimates. Determines bid items and associated quantities.
Develops and updates project schedules. Ensures projects meet local, state and federal regulatory requirements.
Provides expert advice on transportation design, construction, maintenance, and operations.
Makes presentations to the Board of County Commissioners and represents the County at public meetings and workshops.
Prepares, presents, and maintains the department’s operating and capital budgets.
Supports the County Attorney’s Office with providing expert witness testimony.
Addresses inquiries from the County’s elected officials and leaders, and the public regarding transportation capital projects and public infrastructure.
Performs other related duties as required.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to maintain an enthusiastic, self-reliant and self-starting approach to meet job responsibilities.
Ability to anticipate work to be done and initiate proper and acceptable direction for completion of work with a minimum of supervision and instruction.
Knowledge of the Minimum Standards for Design, Construction, and Maintenance Streets and Highways (Florida Greenbook) and the FDOT’s Florida Design Manual.
Knowledge of the Southwest Florida Water Management District’s, U.S. Corps of Engineers and other regulatory agencies’ permitting requirements.
Knowledge of Florida Statutes, as they relate to the operation of County’s government and transportation matters.
Knowledge of federal, state, and private transportation grants.
Knowledge of the County’s Land Development Code.
Knowledge of the practices utilized in government budgeting and cost reduction.
Ability to supervise the work of a large staff of professional, technical, and clerical employees.
Ability to direct and carry out complex oral and written instructions.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with the County Commissioners, County employees, business partners, other governmental agencies, and the public.

Minimum Requirements

PHYSICAL SKILLS:
Ability to communicate effectively using verbal, written and visual communication.

EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering and Ten (10) years of experience in transportation infrastructure planning, design, and construction expertise required. Five (5) years' supervisory experience leading a team of professionals required. Transportation engineering experience preferred.

LICENSES, CERTIFICATIONS OR REGISTRATIONS:
Must possess a valid Florida driver's license. Must possess and maintain Professional Engineer (P.E.) license.

ADA STATEMENT:
A qualified employee or applicant with a disability may be afforded a reasonable accommodation to perform the essential job functions of a position in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE:
Pasco County BOCC is a drug-free workplace in accordance with Federal and Florida law.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE/RECOVERY ACTIVITIES:
All employees will be required to work before, during, or after an emergency. During an emergency, employees may temporarily be assigned to work and perform duties outside the normal scope of their position, location and work schedule to fit the needs of the County and its citizens.

added.description:
Artificial Intelligence Engineer - Vice President

Department: Software Engineering

About The Role

iCapital is seeking a Vice President Artificial Intelligence Engineer to lead the design, development, and delivery of production-grade AI systems that drive measurable business outcomes across the firm. This individual will own key workstreams and serve as a technical leader, driving system design, mentoring engineers, partnering directly with business stakeholders, and ensuring that AI capabilities are built to production-grade standards of reliability, scalability, and measurability. The ideal candidate is a seasoned engineer with a track record of shipping complex AI systems end-to-end and someone who combines deep technical expertise with strong cross-functional partnership, architectural judgment, and able to operate as a force multiplier for the team. This role is expected to bring independent judgment on a technical approach, a bias toward delivery, and able to translate ambiguous business needs into well-scoped, well-executed solutions.

Responsibilities

Lead the architecture and delivery of production AI systems, including document intelligence (IDP), intelligent knowledge systems, agentic orchestration, conversational AI, and generative AI applications, to power internal and external business processes, digital experiences, and workflow automation at scale.
Own AI projects end-to-end, from problem scoping and stakeholder alignment through solution design, implementation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement, delivering tangible business outcomes with a track record of consistent, high-quality delivery.
Drive technical design and architectural decisions for the team, including API design, system decomposition, evaluation strategy, and infrastructure patterns, establishing standards that raise the quality bar across the AI/ML platform.
Architect and champion robust evaluation frameworks for AI systems, defining statistically sound, problem-specific metrics, curating benchmark datasets, and enforcing strict versioning to ensure reproducibility and continuous improvement.
Partner directly with cross-functional stakeholders, including the Product, Operations, Legal, and Business teams, to identify AI opportunities, translate requirements into technical plans, and communicate tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations clearly.
Mentor and develop engineers on the team through code review, design review, pair problem-solving, and knowledge sharing, acting as a technical role model and raising the overall capability of the group.
Identify systemic problems and propose solutions, proactively improving team processes, tooling, and infrastructure to reduce technical debt and increase development velocity.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience developing and deploying production AI/ML systems, including cloud-native solutions on AWS or similar platforms, with a proven track record of delivering complex applications from design through production
Strong proficiency in Python and software engineering best practices, including source control, CI/CD, testing, documentation, and the development of scalable, maintainable software
Deep expertise building production AI solutions, including LLM applications, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), conversational AI, document intelligence, and agentic workflows, with hands-on experience using modern AI frameworks, tooling, and protocols such as MCP and A2A
Experience designing, deploying, and operating end-to-end machine learning pipelines, including model training, deployment, monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement in production environments
Strong foundation in statistics, experimentation, data quality, and AI system evaluation, with experience developing benchmarks, defining performance metrics, analyzing errors, and optimizing systems for accuracy, reliability, scalability, cost, and latency
Experience leading technical design and architectural decisions, conducting code and design reviews, mentoring engineers, and driving engineering excellence across teams
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical solutions, collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, and communicate complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Experience spanning multiple AI domains, including LLM systems, document intelligence, and ML platforms or infrastructure
Experience in financial services or FinTech, particularly within document-heavy, regulated, or compliance-sensitive environments is preferred
Contributions to open-source projects, technical publications, conference presentations, patents, or other demonstrated thought leadership in applied AI and machine learning is preferred

Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $170,000 to $210,000. iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO).

We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday.

added.title: Senior Manager : Tax Technology Implementations
added.description:
About The Team

The Tax Technology team owns the technology behind what happens on our platform. We build and run the systems that calculate indirect tax on every transaction — and we go well beyond that. We build the automations and implementations the direct tax team relies on, we support data operations across the tax function, and we develop the tooling and efficiencies that make the wider Tax Force faster. We are a global team spanning three brands: DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo.

That reach also makes us one of the most dependency-heavy systems in the company. More than eight separate billing domains feed into our tax services, each with its own architecture, roadmap, and engineering team — and all of them have to work.

Getting this right is not optional. Tax has to be correct on every order, the first time. Getting it wrong means incorrect charges to real customers, restatement risk, and audit exposure. We are looking for someone who can hold the whole picture and make it land.

About The Role

The Senior Manager, Tax Technology Implementations reports to the Director of Tax Technology and owns the technical implementation plan between the various domains and our indirect tax calculation service.

You have a deep understanding of the indirect Tax subject matter and also the technical partner to the engineering team. You will translate indirect tax requirements into things engineers can build, and you will own the single consolidated plan that tells Tax and Engineering leadership where the program actually stands.

You will influence partner teams with your understanding of the problem and source of truth of a trusted plan. You make it easy for partner teams to do the right thing.

This role owns the tax outcome of implementations— the requirements, the design judgment, and the technical calls that determine whether it works.

Requirements and design.
Author tax requirements and acceptance criteria that engineers build against and that hold up under audit. Review design docs and push back where a design won't scale to the tax rules coming.

Scope and sequencing.
Define what's in and out for each integration, own the critical path, and drive what ships when. When a team slips, know within a day what it means downstream — and bring options.

Roadmap influence.
Get tax work prioritized onto eight other teams' roadmaps and defend it when it's bumped — making this a collaboration between the engineering, product teams and tax.

Launch and operational readiness.
Define testing, monitoring, and rollout, set go/no-go and rollback criteria, and make sure each integration lands with runbooks, alerting, and a clear steady-state owner.

Risk.
Own the risk register and escalate with a recommendation attached. Be the person who saw it coming.

Running the program.
Maintain the integrated plan as the source of truth and keep the decision cadence across Tax, Product, Engineering, and Data — reporting status to senior leadership in a format they trust.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

Have visibility across the entire business, solving genuinely complex problems across many domains with both engineering and non-engineering partners.
Own an end-to-end program rather than a slice of one, with real consequences and real scope.
Work closely with engineers to shape design decisions, not just receive them.
Build the connective tissue for a program that spans three brands and multiple jurisdictions.
Be supported by Anthropics Claude suite of tooling and an extensive tax data mart to speed up analysis, planning, and daily operations.
Grow a team and a function that is still being defined.

We're excited about you because…

8+ years in a corporate tax department, public accounting, or technology consulting
Global or multi-country indirect tax implementation experience, and familiarity with non-US indirect tax regimes.
Hands-on experience implementing Marketplace Facilitator laws across jurisdictions.
Program or project management experience across multiple dependent engineering teams, including building plans, milestones, and dependency maps, and driving them to completion.
Direct engagement with engineering teams on product development, with working knowledge of software development processes. You can read a technical design document and tell whether it will hold.
Experience defining testing and monitoring strategies for systems where correctness matters.
Strong analytical skills, high organization, and real attention to detail, with the ability to hold both the big picture and the specifics.
Comfort operating without formal authority in a highly collaborative, multi-stakeholder environment. You are not afraid to challenge the status quo, and you do it in a way that keeps partners on your side.

Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

added.title: Chief Information & AI Officer
added.description:
Location: hybrid Atlanta, San Diego & Orlando

Full-time, Executive
Reports to the President

Every lender in the country can buy the same AI models on the same afternoon. Almost none of them have worked out how to put those models to work in a business where a wrong answer is a regulatory event — and, for the owner on the other end, a payroll that does not get made. That is the job.

FairSquare is looking for a Chief Information & AI Officer to lead our technology organization — and to build something most companies our size are still only talking about.

You will own the full technology stack: software engineering, data, infrastructure, security and IT. On top of that, you will own a harder question. In a small-business lending company, which work should AI simply do? Which should AI draft, with a named human accountable for the result? And which should never leave human hands at all? Your answer has to hold up three ways at once — for a regulator, for a funding partner, and for the business owner waiting on a decision.

Nobody is going to hand you that answer. You will be the executive who collaborates with the team to define it, builds the operating model and the guardrails that make it real, defends it to the Board and to our regulators and funding partners, and then proves — with evidence, not anecdotes — that it works. You will raise the obstacles early, while they are still cheap to fix, and own the outcome either way.

If you believe the durable advantage in AI belongs to the companies that make it accountable rather than the ones that adopt it first, we should talk.

About FairSquare

FairSquare is a technology-driven financial services company serving small businesses across the United States. We began with a singular focus to bring accessible working capital to our nation’s small businesses and have evolved into a full suite of financial products and the ability to cater to every business need. We combine capital, data and technology to get funding into the hands of business owners quickly and responsibly. Founded in 1999, our subsidiary brands offer a range of diverse financing options from premier small business loans to self-service digital lending platforms that support the needs of our customers throughout every stage of their business journey.

The Role

Reporting directly to the President and serving on the executive leadership team, the Chief Information & AI Officer sets and drives FairSquare’s combined technology and artificial intelligence strategy — ensuring our software, infrastructure and AI systems run efficiently, profitably, securely and responsibly.

This is a builder’s seat, not a caretaker’s. You will make executive technology and AI decisions on behalf of the company: owning the technology and AI budget, aligning investment with our vision and our stakeholders’ needs, sequencing AI use cases against a risk-tiered framework, and uniting software engineering, data science, AI and IT into one team that can actually execute against the strategy you set. You will also lead it the way we expect every leader at FairSquare to lead — commitments owned and delivered on time, problems surfaced before they become surprises, disagreement voiced at the table rather than after the meeting, and full commitment carried forward once a decision is made.

What You Will Do

Set the technology and AI strategy for the enterprise, and keep it tied to our Key Goals and business outcomes rather than to tooling.

Find and deploy the technologies — including AI and machine learning — that create genuine competitive advantage in fintech, and say no to the ones that do not. Curiosity about what is new, discipline about what is worth it.

Stand up and lead an AI Center of Excellence: the central hub that sets standards, shared tooling and playbooks for AI leads embedded across the business — and that spreads what works instead of letting it stay in one team.

Prioritize and sequence AI use cases enterprise-wide against a risk-tiered framework, distinguishing what can be automated outright from what requires human oversight or human judgment alone — and deciding in the customer’s favor when the trade-off is close.

Build the governance that makes speed defensible — model risk management, data protection, quality assurance, fair-lending and regulatory compliance, and explainability and audit standards for AI output.

Own system infrastructure end to end: functionality, resilience, security, and the platforms our AI work depends on.

Define and report the measures that matter — adoption, accuracy, override and correction rates, cycle-time impact and return on investment — and carry that story, good news and bad, to the President and the Board.

Partner across every function to put technology and AI to profitable use: treat internal colleagues as customers, go to the person rather than around them, name the friction you find in a process instead of quietly working around it, and use what you hear back to adjust course.

Coach, develop and retain a distributed team of software, data science, AI and IT professionals — keeping real development plans in place for your leaders and yourself, and working with HR on the AI fluency, reskilling and change management that enterprise AI adoption genuinely requires.

Lead in line with our policies and applicable law: hiring and training, planning and directing work, and developing and rewarding performance.

What You Bring

A bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, data science or a related field; a master’s or PhD in AI/ML is preferred.

At least 10 years in technology roles, including hands-on exposure to AI/ML or data science, and at least 5 years leading people.

A track record of owning budgets and business planning at scale — and of delivering what you committed to, on the date you committed to it.

Strategic range — the ability to set a direction across both the technology and the AI domains, then execute it: consulting widely before you decide, and moving with real urgency once you have.

Deep technical knowledge of cloud platforms, mobile applications and generative AI, and a clear sense of how they apply to financial services and lending.

Real experience with AI governance, model risk management and regulatory compliance — including fair-lending regulation (for example ECOA / Regulation B) and data privacy.

Communication skill that travels: you can explain an AI capability, and its risk, to an engineer and to a director in the same week — and you disagree openly before a decision is made rather than relitigating it afterward.

Leadership and organizational ability across a distributed, cross-functional operating model, with a record of growing people and not only shipping projects — the leaders you have developed are the evidence.

Sound judgment about when AI is the right answer — the confidence to say when it is not, and the self-awareness to name your own blind spots before someone else does.

Why This Role Is Different

Most technology executives inherit a roadmap. You will inherit a mandate.

FairSquare has made a deliberate decision to treat AI as an operating-model question rather than a procurement one — which means the person in this seat gets to redesign how work actually moves through the company, not just buy the software that supports it. Executive leadership and the Board are already engaged and expect to be held to evidence. The budget is real. The scope is the enterprise.

It is also a role with a conscience attached. Every role here touches a customer, and the standard we hold ourselves to is that we can always explain how a decision was made and who was accountable for it. Small businesses risk it all for a dream; we risk it all to make sure they win. If that constraint reads to you as the interesting part of the problem rather than the annoying part, you are the person we are looking for.

Compensation & Location

Salary range: Base Salary: $290K-375K. Position eligible for additional incentives including bonus, equity, 401(k) match, health and welfare benefits, amazing culture, growth opportunity and more.

Location: This position is a Hybrid role and will work from our offices in either: San Diego, CA; Atlanta, GA, or Orlando, FL.

FairSquare is an equal opportunity employer.

This is a pivotal moment for Google SecOps. You will lead the charge in scaling a billion-dollar product from 1,500 to 15,000 customers, requiring unprecedented architectural resilience and operational excellence. Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $364000 - $505000 (USD) + 40% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Define and execute the long-term technical vision and strategy for the Google SecOps engineering organization. Partner with product management, research, and other engineering teams to ensure the successful delivery of impactful customer value through Google Cloud Security products and services.
Build, mentor, and lead a global engineering team, fostering a culture of innovation and high performance.
Partner closely with product management leadership to ensure seamless product integration and a roadmap that meets the evolving needs of the security market.
Directly oversee the architectural migration from F1/Spanner to BigQuery, ensuring zero-downtime and enhanced performance for our customers.
Lead the technical development of the Agentic SOC initiative, driving the integration of advanced AI and automation into the core analyst workflow.

About The Team

The Tax Technology team owns the technology behind what happens on our platform. We build and run the systems that calculate indirect tax on every transaction — and we go well beyond that. We build the automations and implementations the direct tax team relies on, we support data operations across the tax function, and we develop the tooling and efficiencies that make the wider Tax Force faster. We are a global team spanning three brands: DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo.

That reach also makes us one of the most dependency-heavy systems in the company. More than eight separate billing domains feed into our tax services, each with its own architecture, roadmap, and engineering team — and all of them have to work.

Getting this right is not optional. Tax has to be correct on every order, the first time. Getting it wrong means incorrect charges to real customers, restatement risk, and audit exposure. We are looking for someone who can hold the whole picture and make it land.

About The Role

The Senior Manager, Tax Technology Implementations reports to the Director of Tax Technology and owns the technical implementation plan between the various domains and our indirect tax calculation service.

You have a deep understanding of the indirect Tax subject matter and also the technical partner to the engineering team. You will translate indirect tax requirements into things engineers can build, and you will own the single consolidated plan that tells Tax and Engineering leadership where the program actually stands.

You will influence partner teams with your understanding of the problem and source of truth of a trusted plan. You make it easy for partner teams to do the right thing.

This role owns the tax outcome of implementations— the requirements, the design judgment, and the technical calls that determine whether it works.

Requirements and design.
Author tax requirements and acceptance criteria that engineers build against and that hold up under audit. Review design docs and push back where a design won't scale to the tax rules coming.

Scope and sequencing.
Define what's in and out for each integration, own the critical path, and drive what ships when. When a team slips, know within a day what it means downstream — and bring options.

Roadmap influence.
Get tax work prioritized onto eight other teams' roadmaps and defend it when it's bumped — making this a collaboration between the engineering, product teams and tax.

Launch and operational readiness.
Define testing, monitoring, and rollout, set go/no-go and rollback criteria, and make sure each integration lands with runbooks, alerting, and a clear steady-state owner.

Risk.
Own the risk register and escalate with a recommendation attached. Be the person who saw it coming.

Running the program.
Maintain the integrated plan as the source of truth and keep the decision cadence across Tax, Product, Engineering, and Data — reporting status to senior leadership in a format they trust.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

Have visibility across the entire business, solving genuinely complex problems across many domains with both engineering and non-engineering partners.
Own an end-to-end program rather than a slice of one, with real consequences and real scope.
Work closely with engineers to shape design decisions, not just receive them.
Build the connective tissue for a program that spans three brands and multiple jurisdictions.
Be supported by Anthropics Claude suite of tooling and an extensive tax data mart to speed up analysis, planning, and daily operations.
Grow a team and a function that is still being defined.

We're excited about you because…

8+ years in a corporate tax department, public accounting, or technology consulting
Global or multi-country indirect tax implementation experience, and familiarity with non-US indirect tax regimes.
Hands-on experience implementing Marketplace Facilitator laws across jurisdictions.
Program or project management experience across multiple dependent engineering teams, including building plans, milestones, and dependency maps, and driving them to completion.
Direct engagement with engineering teams on product development, with working knowledge of software development processes. You can read a technical design document and tell whether it will hold.
Experience defining testing and monitoring strategies for systems where correctness matters.
Strong analytical skills, high organization, and real attention to detail, with the ability to hold both the big picture and the specifics.
Comfort operating without formal authority in a highly collaborative, multi-stakeholder environment. You are not afraid to challenge the status quo, and you do it in a way that keeps partners on your side.

GridUnity is the industry leader in interconnection life cycle management, delivering cutting-edge software solutions that eliminate bottlenecks in the interconnection process and accelerate the transition to a more affordable, sustainable, and resilient energy future.

Our Mission

We unite all grid interconnection stakeholders on a single platform that converts centralized data into actionable intelligence and accelerates the transition to a reliable, sustainable, and cost-efficient electric grid.

GridUnity is a trusted partner to leading utilities, grid operators, and policymakers. Our technology solutions tackle the interconnection queue backlog by significantly reducing processing times. Whether cutting transmission interconnection timelines from years to months or enabling distribution applications to be processed within a day, we help accelerate energy projects at every scale.

Our Vision

Energizing the planet with a faster, smarter, and more sustainable grid.

About The Role

This position reports to GridUnity’s Strategic Product Officer and will be responsible for evolving the strategy and roadmap for the technical capabilities the GridUnity Intelligence Platform provides to our national customer base. You will partner with GridUnity’s application product owners to ensure each new application launched and supported by GridUnity and its partner network leverages the platform in the most efficient manner.

You do this by helping set the vision for the platform components and capabilities and then keeping stakeholders aligned around the vision, the strategy for realizing this vision, and collaborating with the application product owners to ensure product management's approach to customer needs is clear to the engineering team. You ensure the engineering team maintains a well-defined understanding of the prioritized components, backlog and goals for each development increment, which is delivered through iterative Agile development. As the owner of both strategy and tactics, you will be a member of the Agile development team by specifying product requirements, planning development iterations, reviewing development progress, and accepting deliverables for release to customers.

Platform strategy & roadmap

Own the strategic roadmap for GridUnity's Intelligence Platform components and coordinate delivery timing with the Director of Product Management.
Balance platform prioritization against the feature velocity Product Owners need; present and defend those trade-offs to leadership.
Set platform success metrics — API adoption, integration uptime/reliability, time-to-build for a new module, PO/developer satisfaction — and report against them.

Evolve and govern the developer API portal so internal Product teams and external partners can build against the growing set of platform capabilities.

Define integration requirements, SLAs, and support models with engineering, security, and customer-facing teams.

Sequence platform-hardening work that protects utility and regulator customers' data.
